title: Session-aware usage rollback reconciler and idempotent patcher
creator: Asha Kumar
description:
Problem: When long-lived user sessions (websocket or multi-call SDK sessions) encounter partial failures or client-side retries, token usage records are sometimes duplicated or left in an inconsistent intermediate state in the token_ledger. Current reconciliation jobs run epochally and assume idempotent per-request records; they do not reliably detect session-bound rollbacks where a previously reported increment must be retracted or merged.

Goal: Implement a session-aware rollback reconciler and idempotent patcher that can consume a stream of session events (start, checkpoint, commit, abort) and apply correct adjustments to the token ledger with audit metadata. The reconciler must:
- Accept both event-sourced (Kinesis) and batch (Parquet/BigQuery) inputs.
- Detect out-of-order events and apply causal ordering heuristics based on event timestamps and sequence IDs.
- Support an idempotent patch API for downstream jobs and customer exports so repeated runs do not double-bill.
- Emit rich provenance metadata (source, session_id, checkpoint_id, reconciler_run_id) for traceability and for Console to show disputed tokens.

Non-goals: This ticket does not change token pricing logic or introduce billing refunds — it focuses on ledger correctness and metadata for follow-up manual/automated billing adjustments.
acceptance_criteria: Reconciler consumes session event stream and produces delta records that reconcile to a single canonical token count per session checkpoint.
Idempotent patch API accepts a dedupe-key and guarantees at-most-once application for reconciler patches within a 30-day window.
Unit and integration tests demonstrating recovery from out-of-order events and duplicate event delivery.
Reconciler emits a reconciliation audit record to events.audit_stream and updates console-test dashboard with before/after token deltas.
No increase in incorrect customer charges in the staging billing simulator (0 regressions in 10k simulated sessions).
tasks: Design session event schema and add checkpoint/sequence fields to existing websocket SDK emitters (coord with SDK team).
Prototype streaming reconciler logic in a test harness using local Kinesis emulator and sample event replays.
Implement idempotent patch API backed by dedupe table with TTL and implement optimistic concurrency checks.
Add provenance fields to token_ledger schema and migration plan for backfilling minimal metadata for last 90 days.
Create integration test with billing-sim to validate net token counts and ensure no double-application under retries.
Add dashboard panels for reconciliation run success/failure rates and per-customer disputed-token counts.
Write runbook for on-call to diagnose reconciler failures and initiate manual rollback/repair flows.
notes: 10/09: Scoped ticket; decided to prioritize streaming first, with batch backfill as a separate job to avoid long-run migrations.
10/15: Spike showed out-of-order events are common when mobile clients reconnect; plan to use (session_id, seq_id) pair and server-side monotonic seq on reconnect.
10/22: Agreed with SDK team to add checkpoint commit/abort primitives to JS/Python SDKs; SDK PR needs backwards compatibility where seq_id absent maps to legacy path.
10/29: Security review waived for initial reconciler (no PII addition); will re-request if audit metadata includes new customer identifiers.
11/02: Initial streaming reconciler MVP deployed to staging with canary on 2% of sessions; observed a 0.6% reduction in duplicate token articles in staging ledger.
comments: Miguel Torres (2025-10-10): Initial spike completed, pushing prototype branch for early review. https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/5821
Claire Nguyen (2025-10-18): Reviewed schema changes; suggest adding reconciler_run_id to make cross-job traceback easier.
Asha Kumar (2025-10-25): Added billing-sim test vectors for disconnect/reconnect flows. See billing-sim:tests/session_replay/*.json
SRE Pager (2025-11-01): Canary run healthy; CPU spike observed on reconciliation burst, planning horizontal shard increase for stream processors.
implementation_notes: Prefer Kinesis (streaming) for near-real-time correction, with a Beam pipeline producing reconciler deltas to a dedupe topic.
Use a small DynamoDB dedupe table keyed by dedupe_key = sha256(session_id|checkpoint_id|source) with 30d TTL for at-most-once semantics.
Patch API should accept a patch manifest (list of ledger_ids -> delta) and return a patch_id; clients must persist patch_id to avoid reapplying.
Backfill plan: run batch reconciliation over last 90 days, emit patch manifests but gate apply with a manual approval in Console for high-risk customers.
